title: Probabilistic smoothing and weighted-metric fusion for rollout guards
author: Maya Chen
release_notes:
- Add probabilistic exponential smoothing for noisy latency/throughput signals
- Add weighted metric fusion layer that computes a single canary score from multiple signals
- Backfill baseline recalibration script and offline simulator for validation
- Canary policy updated to require confidence threshold and minimum stable window (non-breaking)
description:
Context: Our current canary detector can be hypersensitive to transient spikes (short-lived latency blips, bursty traffic drops) which led to a handful of noisy rollbacks during aggressive rollouts. This PR implements two complementary techniques to reduce false positives while preserving sensitivity to real regressions: (1) probabilistic smoothing (an uncertainty-aware EMA) per metric to avoid overreacting to single-sample spikes, and (2) a weighted-metric fusion layer that combines latency percentiles, throughput drop, error rate, and queue depth into a single 'fused canary score' with configurable weights derived from historical feature importance.

Summary of changes: 1) core detection library (perf_canary/detector) now exposes SmoothingWindow and ConfidenceEstimators and computes per-metric posterior distributions instead of single-point samples; 2) fusion module (perf_canary/fusion.py) implements a logistic-weighted aggregator with normalization and historical-weight calibration; 3) canary policy schema extended with "min_confidence" and "fusion_weights" and wiring in the orchestration layer (orchestrator/canary_policy.go); 4) offline simulator and backfill (tools/canary_simulator) to validate detection precision/recall and re-calibrate thresholds using historical traces; 5) dashboards and runbook updates (docs/observability/canary-metrics.md).

Why this design: Probabilistic smoothing lets the detector express uncertainty (wide posterior during cold starts/bursts) so the rollout guard can require a minimum confidence when deciding to fail. Weighted fusion keeps the system flexible: teams can tune which signals matter most for their workload (e.g., latency-heavy vs throughput-sensitive). The offline simulator helps pick weight priors and fusion thresholds from historical false-positive/false-negative tradeoffs.

Commits (high-level): - feat(detector): add probabilistic EMA and confidence estimator - feat(fusion): implement logistic-weighted metric aggregator and calibration routines - feat(sim): add offline canary simulator and backfill script - perf(tests): add unit and integration tests for fusion/detector - docs: canary policy schema, migration guide, observability dashboard panels

Files changed (high level): perf_canary/detector.py, perf_canary/fusion.py, orchestrator/canary_policy.go, tools/canary_simulator/main.go, docs/observability/canary-metrics.md, tests/test_fusion.py, tests/test_detector_confidence.py, charts/canary-values.yaml, scripts/backfill/recalibrate_baselines.py

Small illustrative snippet (fusion scoring pseudocode):

  score = 0.0
  for metric in metrics:
    norm = (metric.value - metric.baseline_mean) / metric.baseline_std
    contribution = sigmoid(alpha * norm) * weight[metric.name]
    score += contribution
  fused_score = score / sum(weights)

Rollout guard change: the canary policy now evaluates fused_score and a confidence estimate. The policy fails a canary if fused_score > threshold AND confidence >= min_confidence for stable_window seconds (configurable). This reduces flips on transient spikes while keeping sensitivity to sustained regressions.

Testing and validation: unit tests cover calibration and edge cases (zero-variance baselines, missing signals). The offline simulator ran historical replay over the last 90 days of production traces (sampled) to evaluate precision/recall for a range of thresholds and weight priors; simulator results are included in tools/canary_simulator/output/ and summarized in the PR artifacts. CI includes a perf-regression check which compares detection latency/false-positive rate against the current baseline; this PR passes the check.

Migration & rollout plan: feature gated behind "perf_fusion_v1" flag. Plan: 1) Stage rollout to 10% of clusters for 48h with elevated telemetry retention, 2) run simulator-based calibration and adjust default weights, 3) expand to 50% for 24h, 4) full rollout with automatic fallback to previous detector if false-positive rate exceeds 1% over 6h. We rolled this sequence out in staging and observed a 62% reduction in noisy rollbacks for the test cohort.

Risks & mitigation: the main risk is mis-calibrated weights causing reduced sensitivity. Mitigations: conservative default weights, feature-flagged rollout, and an automatic rollback trigger at the canary controller level if false-positive or missed-regression metrics degrade beyond threshold.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the fusion layer model-agnostic (no ML model dependencies) to avoid infra complexity; however the calibration module emits CSVs suitable for later ML-based weight tuning if we opt in.

Related: Linear ENG-6821 (canary stability work), ENG-6903 (canary simulator enhancements).

review_thread:
Alden Park: Can we get more detail on the confidence estimator math and edge behavior?
Author (Maya): Added detailed comments and a reference test (test_detector_confidence.py) that validates behavior at low-sample counts and zero-variance baselines. Confidence is computed from posterior std via a normalized inverse-variance transform.
Riley Gomez: Simulator looks good — did you try different weight priors?
Author: Yes — simulator run artifacts include 5 priors (uniform, latency-heavy, throughput-heavy, error-weighted, learned-from-history). Default uses the history-based prior but teams can override in policy.
Samira Patel (LGTM): Please add a short runbook entry to docs/observability and ensure the charts expose per-signal contributions (now included).
Author: Addressed — added dashboard panels and runbook section; CI passed on re-run.
Merge: Approved by all reviewers and merged via squash.
